articles.title: Jalen Hurts on Injured Reserve With Superficial Blood Clot, Latest on Eagles QB's Timeline to Return
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport had previously reported that injured reserve wasn't in the initial plans.

"The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of IR, which would sideline him for a minimum of four weeks," according to Schefter and Rapoport. "In general, the minimum timeframe for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources say."

However, after consulting with doctors, that decision has changed.

The Eagles released a statement on the situation on Thursday:

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

Hurts previously dealt with a calf injury that he suffered during a Week 4 matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, but was able to play through it in Philadelphia's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5.

Availability hasn't been a major issue for Hurts throughout his career, as he appeared in 48 of a possible 51 games from 2023-25.

This season, the 28-year-old has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in five games/

Hurts has also continued to make plays with his legs, rushing for 107 yards and one touchdown.

Philadelphia (2-3) is looking to clinch its sixth consecutive playoff appearance and third straight division crown. After capturing a Super Bowl title during the 2024 season, the Eagles suffered a disappointing elimination in the Wild Card round last year.

With Hurts out, backup passer Tanner McKee will likely fill in.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Injury Update, Latest Rumors on WR's Status for Patriots' Game vs. Jets
articles.summary: New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and reportedly is expected to play Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and reportedly is expected to play Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets.

Brown updated reporters on his status on Thursday:

"I feel pretty good," Brown said. "It's one step at a time with me, each and every day, just trying to increase my [workload], and just see how I respond each and every day. But I feel good, on the grass, practicing, working on the sides a little more."

"He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple of days," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good, and his ability to be around the guys in the meetings and then also focus on his rehab and treat everything as a pro."

Brown, 29, was New England's major offseason acquisition, coming over in an offseason trade from the Philadelphia Eagles. But he suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 1 loss against the Seattle Seahawks and his 21-day practice window was opened this week.

Getting back the three-time Pro Bowler and one-time Super Bowl champion will obviously boost an offense that was already starting to find its groove again in recent weeks, although the timeline for Brown's return remains uncertain.

Another offseason addition, Romeo Doubs, has led the passing attack in Brown's absence. He's caught 13 passes for 219 yards and two scores. Drake Maye has also relied on Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and tight end Hunter Henry, and the Patriots have run the ball well.

But Brown provides a downfield threat and is one of the best contested-catch weapons in football. Upon his return, he'll immediately be the top priority in the passing game and should create opportunities for his teammates as well.

"I think you see it in the NBA," Maye told reporters. "It's probably the closest thing that I can think of. When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So, it's kind of like playing receiver and with a guy like that—we've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses."

articles.title: New Shedeur Sanders Trade Rumors Leak After Browns QB Hires Travis Hunter's Agent
articles.summary: Even though Shedeur Sanders recently hired an agent for the first time in his NFL career after previously representing himself, there's nothing to indicate he is leaving the Cleveland Browns imminently.
articles.body:
Even though Shedeur Sanders recently hired an agent for the first time in his NFL career after previously representing himself, there's nothing to indicate he is leaving the Cleveland Browns imminently.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , citing discussions with people around the league and Browns officials, it would be a surprise if Sanders were to be moved prior to the trade deadline.

Sanders' new agent, Adie von Gontard of Young Money APAA Sports, also represents Travis Hunter. Sanders and Hunter were teammates for three seasons in college.

A fifth-round pick in the 2025 draft, Sanders rookie contract runs through the 2028 season. He will become extension eligible after the 2027 campaign.

Cleveland's quarterback situation has quieted down somewhat because Deshaun Watson has had moments when he has looked okay. His 268 passing yards in a Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers were his most in a game since Sept. 24, 2023.

Last week was a significant step back for Watson, who finished 15-of-33 for 155 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in a 17-12 loss to the New York Jets.

The Browns being 3-2 so far has also taken some pressure off head coach Todd Monken.

Sanders' lone appearance so far this season was in Week 3 when he threw one pass in a win over the Carolina Panthers after Watson took a hard hit on the previous play.

One reason the Browns might not be looking to trade Sanders right now, according to Jones, is general manager Andrew Berry has "great affection" for the second-year quarterback.

Sanders started seven games as a rookie, leading the Browns to a 3-4 record. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight appearances last season.

articles.title: New Rumors on Bo Nix After Ryan Fitzpatrick Ripped Broncos QB in Viral Video After Win vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Despite Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix's poor play during Thursday night's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks, and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick's scathing evaluation of his performance, Nix is reportedly still looked at highly within the Broncos organization.
articles.body:
Despite Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix's poor play during Thursday night's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks, and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick's scathing evaluation of his performance, Nix is reportedly still looked at highly within the Broncos organization.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, "Nobody in the Broncos' building is more competitive than Bo Nix. He's a hard worker. Teammates love him."

Pelissero relayed that information after Fitzpatrick, who is an analyst for the NFL on Prime Video, blasted Nix on Thursday night:

Among other things, Fitzpatrick said, "Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing quarterback right now."

The 26-year-old Nix exceeded expectations over his first two NFL seasons, taking the Broncos to the playoffs twice, including the AFC Championship Game last season, and throwing for a total of 7,706 yards, 54 touchdowns and 23 interceptions, while also rushing for 786 yards and nine scores.

Although the Broncos have persevered against a tough schedule so far this season to get off to a 4-2 start, there is no doubt that Nix has regressed compared to his first two campaigns.

In addition to completing a career-low 60.3 percent of his passes, Nix has thrown for just 1,049 yards, six touchdowns and three picks through six games.

Per Doug Clawson of CBS Sports, Nix is currently having the most conservative start to a season by a quarterback over the past two decades in terms of air yards per attempt:

That conservatism was on full display Thursday, as Nix went 17-of-27 for 107 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

As seen in the NFL Next Gen Stats passing chart from Thursday's game, Nix did not complete a pass of 10 yards or more down the field, and seven of his completions occurred behind the line of scrimmage:

He was aided by an interception thrown by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold in overtime, which essentially put the Broncos in field goal range and allowed them to win the game.

Nix has never been one to consistently attack defenses down the field, averaging 6.7 yards per attempt as a rookie and 6.4 yards per attempt last season.

However, he is sitting at just 5.6 yards per attempt so far this season, which is surprising given that the Broncos upgraded their receiving corps during the offseason by acquiring Jaylen Waddle from the Miami Dolphins.

It should be noted that Nix has dealt with some turmoil in the coaching ranks, as offensive coordinator Davis Webb began the season as the offensive play-caller before getting supplanted by head coach Sean Payton.

Payton called the plays over Nix's first two seasons, and although that familiarity didn't seem to help much on Thursday, perhaps that will change as time goes on.

articles.title: Texans 'Aware' How Marvin Harrison Jr.'s 'Effort' Looked on Tape, New NFL Rumors Reveal After Trade
articles.summary: The Houston Texans aren't concerned about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s play during his time with the Arizona Cardinals after they gave up a second-round pick to acquire the veteran wide receiver.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans aren't concerned about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s play during his time with the Arizona Cardinals after they gave up a second-round pick to acquire the veteran wide receiver.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Texans are "aware" of the "lack of effort" that showed up on Harrison's tape at times during his time in Arizona and have confidence that won't carry over in part because he is because he gets to play with his former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud:

"The Texans are aware of what Harrison's tape in Arizona looked like. And though he's been with the team for less than a week, there have been no signs within the organization that the lack of effort seen on tape has traveled with him to Houston (or, for that matter, London, where the Texans will play the Jaguars on Sunday).

"The flow of the game will likely dictate Harrison's snaps, but I'm told he has picked things up well and will do more as the year goes along. What will be interesting to see is how he adapts to playing opposite the X receiver, a position Nico Collins holds.

"'We're hoping that because of the dynamic with his college quarterback and a change of scenery, it will unlock him,' one team source says."

Harrison was regarded as one of the best receiver prospects in recent memory going into the 2024 NFL draft. He had an outstanding two-year run at Ohio State with 144 receptions for 2,474 yards and 28 touchdowns in 25 games from 2022 to '23.

B/R's NFL scouting department described Harrison as a "slam-dunk prospect" and cited A.J. Green as a comparison for his style of play.

The Cardinals made Harrison the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 draft. He was the highest-drafted wide receiver for the franchise since Larry Fitzgerald was selected third overall in 2004.

Harrison had a solid rookie season with 885 yards and eight touchdowns in 17 games, but things have fallen off dramatically since then. He has 693 yards and four touchdowns in 16 games since the start of the 2025 season.

There have been clips posted from games this season that appear to show Harrison not going at full speed, though Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur disagreed with the notion he wasn't playing hard.

It seems clear based on the trade package that the Texans believe a change of scenery and playing with a quarterback Harrison has familiarity with can turn things around. They gave up a 2027 second-round pick to acquire him from Arizona.

Houston desperately needed help at wide receiver with Jayden Higgins out for the season and Tank Dell still on injured reserve.

Nico Collins has missed time already due to a hamstring injury, though he has looked fine with 174 yards and two touchdowns in two games since returning.

The combination of Stroud at quarterback and Collins being the No. 1 option in the offense should ease some of the pressure on Harrison. He's only 24 and has one more guaranteed year on his rookie contract, so the upside for a Texans team trying to get back on track amid a 1-4 start makes it worth the risk for them.

Harrison will make his Texans debut on Sunday when they play the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts ruled out for Week 6 after blood clot found in his leg, not expected to go on IR
articles.summary: If Hurts were to be placed on IR he would miss at least four weeks.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are not planning on placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after a superficial blood clot was discovered in his leg .

According to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , the Eagles believe the blood clot is treatable and do not feel the need to shut Hurts down for at least four weeks with an IR stint. Both parties are gathering more information and seeking out other medical opinions.

Hurts has already been ruled out for this week's game against the Carolina Panthers.

The Eagles released a statement Thursday saying that Hurts asked the team's training staff to treat his calf on Oct. 8 after being cleated during a game against the Los Angeles Rams days earlier. An ultrasound was performed on Oct. 10 after the team flew to London. The results showed a superficial blood clot, but doctors and medical staff concluded "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play."

The team says Hurts, who did not carry an injury designation before the game, played "without limitation" last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars and was able to practice fully Wednesday after receiving treatment earlier in the week.

A follow-up ultrasound was done Wednesday which "revealed movement in the small blood clot."

Hurts will miss Week 6 and there is currently no timetable for a return. The Eagles said they have been in communication with the NFL regarding the matter.

Tanner McKee, who has played six career NFL games since being drafted in 2023, will be the Eagles' starter.

articles.title: Patriots will reportedly activate receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve after 4-game absence
articles.summary: Brown has been sidelined since suffering a high-ankle sprain during New England's season opener.
articles.body:
Receiver A.J. Brown is expected to play in the New England Patriots' Week 6 matchup with the New York Jets, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Brown, 29, has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots' season opener versus the Seattle Seahawks. He left New England's 13-10 loss in the third quarter after catching three passes for 26 yards, and was placed on injured reserve the next day.

Going on IR meant that Brown would have to sit out for the next four games. Thus, he was eligible to be activated this week. Brown was a limited participant in all three of the Patriots' practice sessions for the week and is listed as questionable for Sunday .

Earlier in the week, head coach Mike Vrabel said "there is a chance" the veteran receiver would be able to return for Week 6.

"Whenever he'll be back, he should help us," Vrabel said on Monday during his weekly appearance on Boston's WEEI. "I hope that he's going to help us, but that remains to be seen yet when he'll be back. So we'll see how he does and move from there."

Brown's pending return looked like a strong possibility when the Patriots placed receiver Mack Hollins on IR prior to Week 5's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Before going on IR, Hollins had the most catches among Patriots wide receivers with 15 for 209 yards. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson and tight end Hunter Henry also have 15 receptions for New England (3-2).

The Patriots acquired Brown during the offseason from the Philadelphia Eagles, in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round selection. Though he had 1,003 receiving yards last season with the Eagles (his lowest total in four seasons), Brown had reportedly grown frustrated with quarterback Jalen Hurts — and the Eagles' offense in general.

That led to Brown being traded before a three-year, $96 million extension kicked in that takes him through the 2029 season.

Brown is in his eighth NFL season, which began with the Tennessee Titans for three years. He was the team's second-round selection (No. 51 overall) out of Ole Miss.

The 6-foot-1 receiver was dealt to the Eagles during the 2022 NFL Draft for first- and fourth-round picks. He subsequently received a four-year, $100 million extension from Philadelphia.

A three-time Pro Bowler and two-time Second-Team All-Pro selection, Brown has 527 career receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns.

articles.title: “It connects my life and childhood to every single game”: How George Kittle’s father keeps him grounded with emotional letters before his important NFL games
articles.summary: George Kittle has plenty of reasons to get fired up before an NFL game.
articles.body: George Kittle has plenty of reasons to get fired up before an NFL game. But for the San Francisco 49ers tight end, one of his most personal pregame routines begins with a letter from his father, Bruce Kittle. The letters go beyond the usual words of encouragement. They connect George to his childhood, remind him of the person he was before NFL fame and help him prepare for the pressure that comes with playing at the highest level.The tradition began during George’s sophomore year at the University of Iowa and continued as his career took off. Before games, he reads his father’s words on the team bus and in the locker room. Over time, those notes grew into detailed stories that bring family memories, football lessons and even The Lord of the Rings into his preparation. How Bruce Kittle turns pregame letters into a personal ritualBruce does not simply tell his son to go out and play well. He thinks carefully about what George needs to hear before each game. In an Athletic report, Bruce explained that the letters reflect his view of how to help his son stay focused.“My letters are my vision of what George needs to hear to keep his head on straight,” Bruce said in the report. He also wants George to “keep his feet on the ground, make sure his ego is in check and be the guy he needs to be for his team.”That message takes on added weight as Kittle grows into one of the NFL’s most recognizable tight ends. The attention around him can be loud, but his father’s letters bring him back to the things that matter to his game: staying humble, trusting his preparation and putting the team first.His mother, Jan, also helps Bruce edit the letters. The notes include pictures, making them more personal than a standard motivational speech. George has described how the tradition has changed over the years.Kittle explained that the letters had evolved from “a pregame hype speech to a pregame story.” He added, “It connects my life and childhood to every single game.” A 12-page letter before the NFC Championship GameBruce’s letters can get remarkably detailed. Before the 49ers faced the Green Bay Packers in the NFC Championship Game on January 19, 2020, he wrote George a 12-page letter. Rather than relying only on football talk, Bruce drew on stories from “The Lord of the Rings”, using its battles and characters to frame the challenge ahead.He also worked NFL Next Gen Stats and analytics into his writing. The idea was to give George useful details while helping him picture the challenge in a way that made sense to him.Still, the letters were not simply about getting George fired up. Bruce wanted his son to stay calm when the stakes rose. As he explained in the same report, “To me, the bigger the stakes, the more stillness you need to really excel at a higher level.”That approach offers a glimpse into the preparation behind Kittle’s intensity on the field. Fans see the celebrations, physical blocks and big plays. articles.summary: Despite the embarrassing moment for the Washington Commanders at the end of overtime last week resulting in a tie against the New York Giants, head coach Dan Quinn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job.
articles.body:
Despite the embarrassing moment for the Washington Commanders at the end of overtime last week resulting in a tie against the New York Giants, head coach Dan Quinn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Commanders owner Josh Harris has "never been a believer in midseason coaching changes" and the expectation is Quinn will get the chance to turn things around starting on Monday night against the San Francisco 49ers:

"Commanders owner Josh Harris has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes. But in the wake of last week's overtime debacle in a tie with the Giants (which we talked about in depth on The Ringer NFL Show) he'll be paying close attention to how Dan Quinn's team responds Monday night at San Francisco."

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones added that Quinn, Jayden Daniels and offensive coordinator David Blough all addressed the team this week following the Giants' debacle to take accountability for the final sequence:

"Quinn spoke to the entire team Monday, telling them that everything starts with him and that he should have been better. The secondary message was that while everyone has to be accountable, everyone should hold others accountable, too. Daniels and Blough each addressed the offense individually."

articles.title: NFL rumors: Will Josh Jacobs start for Packers in potential Week 7 return?
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers are finally set to have Josh Jacobs back in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. The running back, who had been in the NFL Commissioner’s...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are finally set to have Josh Jacobs back in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. The running back, who had been in the NFL Commissioner's Exempt list to start the season due to a domestic violence arrest, will officially be removed from the list on Monday.

According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Jacobs is set to start immediately upon his return to the lineup against the Lions.

The Packers have gone 3-2 in their first five games of the season without Jacobs, and they have clearly missed the Pro Bowl running back's production. The Packers are comfortably in last place in rushing yards per game, averaging just 60.4. The Houston Texans, who are second from bottom, are averaging 19.4 rushing yards per game more.

MarShawn Lloyd has proven to be ineffective during his time as the Packers' lead back. He has rushed for just 112 yards on 40 carries for a paltry 2.8 yards per rush. Second-year back Kaleb Johnson has not been much better with 106 yards on 27 carries. However, Lloyd did star with two touchdowns in the Packers' big 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears.

The lack of a reliable rushing attack has put a lot of pressure on Jordan Love, but the quarterback has been showing signs of improvement . After struggling with his accuracy to start the season, he has been more locked in of late. He's completed an impressive 47 out his last 61 pass attempts (77%) over the last two games.

Jacobs' return would be a major boost to Love and the Packers offense, especially in providing more of a threat in play action.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Injury Alert: A.J. Brown Expected to Play Week 6; Fantasy Fallout for Drake Maye and Patriots
articles.summary: A.J. Brown is expected back from IR. See how his return impacts the fantasy outlook for Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown's Impending Return Changes Fantasy Landscape in New England

Fantasy managers who invested heavily in the New England Patriots' passing game this offseason have spent the last month and a half navigating a turbulent landscape. When blockbuster offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the opening quarter of Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks, it felt like a cruel joke. Sidelined on Injured Reserve for the better part of two months, Brown left fantasy lineups scrambling and forced a heavy burden onto a patchwork receiving corps.

Now, according to reports from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the dark cloud is lifting. The Patriots are expected to activate Brown off Injured Reserve in time for their divisional matchup against the New York Jets. After returning to practice this week and testing his ankle, the star wideout is poised to reclaim his role as the undisputed fantasy stud wide receiver of this offense. While Brown may have a bit of a pitch count that limits his upside to more of a WR2 this week, his fantasy managers absolutely have to start him.

For fantasy football players, this news is an absolute earthquake. Inserting an elite, difference-making alpha back into an active offense changes the math across the entire roster. But how does this dramatic shift impact key offensive pieces like Drake Maye, Romeo Doubs, Hunter Henry, and Demario Douglas? Let's break down the fantasy fallout for Week 6.

For young quarterback Drake Maye, the return of his premier weapon provides an invaluable ceiling boost. Maye has experienced a bumpy start to the season while leaning on a patchwork receiving corps, but a route-running technician of Brown's caliber offers the ultimate safety valve and field-stretcher. With opposing defenses forced to dedicate heavy safety attention to Brown, Maye will benefit from wider throwing windows and softer underneath zones. While Maye has been one of the best fantasy quarterbacks over the last two weeks, his overall upside skyrockets now that he possesses a legitimate go-to option capable of turning simple plays into explosive gains. He has legit overall QB1 upside this week.

Romeo Doubs saw an expanded target share in Brown's absence, but the production has been erratic. With Brown drawing the primary cornerback coverage, Doubs slides back into a more natural secondary role. While he will face lighter defensive coverages, his total target volume will likely decrease, converting him into a high-upside, boom-or-bust flex play for Week 6.

Hunter Henry occupies a uniquely stable position amid this offensive reshuffle. Henry has quietly maintained reliable chemistry with Maye throughout the early weeks of the season, and Brown's presence on the perimeter should only help the veteran tight end. Elite wide receivers stretch defenses both vertically and laterally, opening up lucrative soft spots in the middle of the field where tight ends thrive. Henry retains his status as a steady back-end option, with his red-zone equity actually getting a boost because defenses can no longer focus solely on bracketing tight ends and slot receivers near the goal line. Consider Henry a high-end TE2 with TE1 upside this week.

WR Demario Douglas, New England Patriots

Meanwhile, Demario Douglas faces a more noticeable PPR floor dip. Douglas thrived on manufactured touches and short-area slot volume while the receiving room was decimated, but Brown's return eats directly into those underneath targets, turning Douglas into a game-script-dependent flex play or roster hold. Douglas belongs on the bench outside of deep fantasy leagues this week, and can be thrown back on the waiver wire in most leagues.

articles.title: NFL draft prospects 2027: Players to watch for Florida State vs. Miami
articles.summary: Ten 2027 NFL draft prospects to watch in today’s Florida State at Miami game. Will Darian Mensah be the first player off the board in the spring?
articles.body:
Week 7 of the college football season is here, and it brings a key Florida in-state rivalry game. The Florida State Seminoles head from Tallahassee to South Florida today to face the Miami Hurricanes.

This game obviously has plenty of meaning for our community, with so many people having attended or become fans of either team. It felt like the right time to bring in the Miami Dolphins' perspective and take a closer look at some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could be on the field today.

The game kicks off at 7 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and Disney+.

Duce Robinson, wide receiver (Senior) – Robinson is a huge target – like a bigger-than-the-Dolphins-tight-ends huge target. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 230 pounds, Robinson uses his size to give his quarterback a receiver who will fight for contested passes in a huge catch radius. If he gets his hands on the ball, it is going to be a catch. He is not the most precise route runner, and he does not have the speed to pull away from anyone, so he relies on his size to make the catch rather than speed to create separation. He is probably a day-two prospect who can excel as a possession receiver and redzone target.

Charles Lester III, cornerback (Junior) – Lester is likely a developmental outside cornerback with good size. He is 6-foot-2 and 195 pounds, but he still needs to develop his technique, especially against faster, smaller wide receivers. He needs to clean up his work when receivers cut, but he can coach that up this year and in the NFL. He still has eligibility, so a 2027 return to college is not out of the question, but he could transition to the league, probably as a day-two pick. For Miami, where cornerback depth is a question mark, Lester could be an ideal option.

Ja'Bril Rawls, cornerback (Senior) – Another cornerback with good size (6-foot-1, 180 pounds), Rawls is behind his teammate in draft potential, but the potential for success in the NFL is there. He probably needs to add strength, and his frame suggests he can do that without sacrificing speed. He has the versatility to slide back to safety, which might be the better option. He is not the best tackler, and he will need to clean that up in the NFL, especially if he is expected to step up in run defense. A developmental defensive back option who should contribute on special teams, Rawls is likely a day-three prospect who could rise to the end of day two.

Quintrevion Wisner, running back (Senior) – The former Texas running back moved to Florida State this year after three seasons in Austin. He carried the ball 226 times for 1,064 yards in 2024, but he played only nine games in 2025 due to a hamstring injury. He has 29 carries for 141 yards this season, but is buried on the depth chart, and he has to prove he can be a receiving option out of the backfield before he can be considered a feature running back at the NFL level. He is a day-three depth running back option who can contribute on special teams.

Micahi Danzy, wide receiver (Redshirt sophomore) – Danzy is the smaller receiver on our FSU prospects list, but that is only because Robinson is ridiculously large. Danzy is listed at 6-foot-1 and 195 pounds, and he can line up in multiple roles among the receiving corps. He has track speed, setting the FSU school record in the 400, and started his college career as a running back. He has 19 receptions for 139 yards and two touchdowns this season. He uses his speed to his advantage but needs to keep building his route tree. He is probably a day-three prospect who could use his speed to battle his way into a day-two consideration.

Darian Mensah, quarterback (Redshirt junior) – Mensah is a modern college football player who bounces between teams; he started at Tulane, then spent a year at Duke before moving to Miami this year. He throws with anticipation and makes good decisions, but he does not always work through his progressions and still has to prove he can handle pressure. He does not have the strongest arm and throws great short-to-medium passes, but the ball can die on longer throws at times. He could be the first quarterback off the board this year, potentially as the number one overall pick.

Xavier Lucas, cornerback (Junior) – Lucas might be the ideal press-corner for the NFL. He has the size (6-foot-2, 200 pounds) to disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage and the speed to keep up with the league's vertical threats. He contests passes well, using his size to break up jump balls, but he is more likely to knock the ball away than to come away with an interception. He is a liability on run defense, with seemingly no interest in getting his nose into the mess in front of him; he also needs to clean up his tackling. Lucas has missed the last month of the season with an undisclosed injury, but he is expected to return for tonight's game. He is probably a day-two prospect who is clearly not a finished product and will continue to grow in the NFL. For a Dolphins team in need of defensive secondary help, Lucas could be a key target.

Note: Lucas is the basis of the lawsuit from Wisconsin against Miami. Lucas played his freshman year at Wisconsin under a two-year Name, Image, and Likeness contract. He tried to transfer to Miami for his second season, but Wisconsin refused to enter him into the transfer portal, citing his contract. Lucas dropped out of Wisconsin and enrolled at Miami without entering the NCAA's transfer portal, and Wisconsin is alleging tampering by Miami to entice Lucas to transfer.

Damon Wilson II, edge (Senior) – The Dolphins will likely be highly interested in edge rushers in the 2027 Draft, and Wilson could put himself on the board. At 6-foot-4 and 250 pounds, Wilson has the size and athleticism needed to succeed in the NFL. He uses both speed and power to attack offensive tackles, but he needs to add counter moves to get off the block if his initial move does not win. He also needs to improve his edge-setting against the run. He has the flashes to be great in the NFL, but he hasn't shown the consistency yet. He broke out last year at Missouri with a nine-sack season, and he has tallied 3.5 sacks through the first five games this year, including 2.5 sacks against Clemson a couple of weeks ago. If he can keep up that production, he will be a second-round target who could slide into the end of the first round.

Samson Okunlola, offensive tackle/guard (Redshirt Junior) – Okunlola's potential is projected based on limited playing time at Miami. He did not get regular snaps until last year, when he rotated at left guard all season. He was clean, did not allow a sack, and showed he could be relied on in big spots. He slid out to left tackle this year, and he has been successful there as well – though he has had a penalty issue that needs to be cleaned up. He could bring that versatility to the NFL, allowing teams to use him as either a guard or tackle as needed. At 6-foot-6, 330 pounds, he still brings athleticism to the line and could be an effective mover to lead block in running situations. He is probably a day-two prospect who could start as a depth option at tackle and guard before settling into a starting role as a guard on the line.

Ryan Rodriguez, center (Redshirt Senior) – A sixth-year college player, Rodriguez has played both guard and center at Miami. He has had injury issues, including needing surgery in 2022 and 2024. He is 6-foot-2 and 300 pounds, which is smaller than most NFL interior linemen, but Miami's All-Pro center, Aaron Brewer, is 6-foot-2 and 290 pounds, so that might not be a major concern. He has to prove he can withstand the pressure of an entire season and anchor the line, but he has been instrumental in Miami's success early this year, especially given the turnover the Hurricanes had on the line from last year.

Honorable mention: Jamal Meriweather, tackle – The 6-foot-7, 305-pound Meriweather has a lot of potential and could be a good swing tackle in the NFL, but he has not gotten consistent playing time. He will get on the field at some point and is worth watching, but he is likely a late-round pick or undrafted free agent signing who can continue developing early in his NFL career.

articles.title: Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was listed as a possible trade target for the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Could DK Metcalf end up with the Indianapolis Colts? Recently, Aaron Zacharias of Horseshoe Heroes wrote about wide receivers the Colts need to consider before the NFL Trade Deadline passes. Metcalf, who's currently with the Pittsburgh Steelers , was on the list:

DK Metcalf is the least likely on this list for the Colts' future ambitions, but he's also the most interesting possible target. Either it's the Aaron Rodgers factor, or he's simply not a good fit with the Pittsburgh Steelers; Metcalf has, in any case, not worked out. There is a world where the Steelers could trade Metcalf after just one and a half seasons, or wait until they get a different quarterback next year. That said, if there is any interest in him from other teams, would the Steelers turn it away? The Colts could land a No. 1 target with actual No. 1 target experience."

Without a doubt, Indianapolis needs help at the wide receiver position. Does trading for DK Metcalf make sense?

Analyst Lists DK Metcalf as a Trade Target for the Colts

The Seattle Seahawks drafted DK Metcalf in the second round (64th overall pick) of the 2019 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he caught 58 passes for 900 yards and seven touchdowns. He recorded seven receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles . It was the NFL record for most receiving yards by a rookie in a postseason game.

In 2020, Metcalf finished with 83 receptions for 1,303 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He also made the Pro Bowl and was named a second-team All-Pro.

Metcalf finished the 2023 campaign with 66 receptions for 1,114 yards and eight touchdowns. He was named to the second Pro Bowl of his career that year.

DK Metcalf was later traded to the Steelers in 2025. During his career in Pittsburgh, he has caught 78 passes for 1,075 yards and seven touchdowns.

Metcalf's production has been underwhelming this year. In five games, he has only recorded 19 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown on 37 targets.

The Colts wide receiver room is not elite by any stretch of the imagination. It wouldn't be great even if Alec Pierce was available.

Pierce is currently out with a heel injury, and is reportedly still a few weeks away from returning to the field. The former Cincinnati Bearcat signed a four-year, $114 million extension with the Colts during the offseason. Pierce was supposed to be "The Man" for Indy, but he has only played in two games this season.

Fellow Colts receivers like Josh Downs and newcomer Keenan Allen haven't stepped up in Pierce's absence. The team was rumored to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but the Arizona Cardinals , of course, traded him to the Houston Texans instead.

Should Indy trade for DK Metcalf before this year's November 10 Trade Deadline? The Colts could use a two-time Pro Bowler like Metcalf. Yet, it's unclear what the team would have to give up in a deal. Plus, it's unclear whether the Steelers would even be willing to trade him.

Colts quarterback Daniel Jones would surely love to add DK Metcalf. What quarterback wouldn't want to add another offensive playmaker? Metcalf could team with tight end Tyler Warren and improve the team's pass-catching corps. But it's unlikely that such a trade will happen.

articles.title: Washington Commanders Rumor Offers MAJOR Update on What Gets Dan Quinn Fired in Week 6
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is […]
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is sure to cost Dan Quinn his job as head coach.

After Washington went 12-5 and reached the NFC Championship Game in the 2024 season, it seemed like the team had found the coach who could make them a consistent playoff contender. However, ever since, the Commanders have regressed.

Last season, they finished with a disappointing 5-12 record. Many chalked it up to injuries — specifically to quarterback Jayden Daniels. However, there were some worrisome signs during the 2025 campaign. It put added pressure on the coach to deliver better results in 2026. However, they are 1-3-1 heading into a Week 6 Monday Night Football clash against the San Francisco 49ers .

Their record is bad, but they seemingly hit a low point in the Quinn era last week when the offense completely lost track of how much time was left on the clock in overtime against the New York Giants and blew a chance at a game-winning field goal.

Washington Commanders would need to be blown out by San Francisco 49ers to fire Dan Quinn

It has only reignited the discourse about the 56-year-old's job security and the idea that he could be the first coach fired in-season. However, according to Tom Pelissero, while owner Josh Harris will be "paying close attention" on Monday night, he " has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes ."

That is why the NFL insider added that unless the Commanders suffer a blowout loss (very possible against a very good 49ers team) or there are obvious signs the team has quit on their coach, "expect Quinn to get the rest of the season to show he can get things turned in the right direction."

Furthermore, Daniels threw his support behind his coach after he mismanaged their final drive in Week 5, and the NFL insider claims, "Quinn has always had great command of the locker room."

articles.title: Chiefs need to stay on their toes against winless Chargers
articles.summary: Kansas City has an opportunity to end any hope for Los Angeles to turn this season around and they can’t overlook it.
articles.body:
It's hard to call a division matchup a trap game, but the (4-0) Kansas City Chiefs must avoid overlooking the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon.

According to Tom Pelissero, formerly of NFL Network , now with The Ringer and Netflix , the Chargers are "rejecting trade calls" because the team believes it is close to turning it around after an 0-5 start. There are no plans for "a fire sale."

That narrative could change if the Chiefs take care of business this weekend, but if Kansas City lets Los Angeles get its bounceback performance and pick up a win in the AFC West along the way, it could be the turning point the Chargers need to regroup.

Head coach Andy Reid understands the Chargers' desperation. A Reid-led Chiefs team once started 1-5 before ripping off enough consecutive wins to make the postseason in 2015.

During his press conference on Friday, Reid warned that Kansas City needs to stay alert and avoid getting caught off guard by an offensive mind looking to manufacture a win with a lengthy injury report .

"Well, you expect the unexpected," Reid said when asked about Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. "He's a sharp mind and very creative, so you've got to be on your toes. He does a nice job. (Chargers Head Coach) Jim (Harbaugh), likewise. I mean, you have two guys in there that are real good football guys, offensive minds."

Los Angeles will be without its two starting offensive tackles — Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater — along with its top wideout this year: Tre Harris. It's hard to know what the unit could look like with all the injuries, and the Chargers could play into the ambiguity to pull off a major upset.

With their season at a clear pivot point ahead of a Week 7 bye, Los Angeles will go all-out for a win in Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday. On offense, defense and special teams, the Chiefs must be prepared for anything, because the Chargers will play like they have nothing to lose.

articles.title: “He is ready to go”: Travis Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs role take a significant turn as Dave Toub prepares him for an emergency position beyond tight end duties
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has another job to prepare for as the Kansas City Chiefs look to protect themselves against a special teams emergency.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has another job to prepare for as the Kansas City Chiefs look to protect themselves against a special teams emergency. The veteran tight end already carries a big workload on offense, but special teams coordinator Dave Toub wants him ready to step in at long snapper if the team needs him.The plan comes during a significant stretch of Kelce’s career. The 2026 season could be his last in the NFL, and the Chiefs are off to a 4-0 start. Currently, Kelce remains focused on his usual role. However, an injury to the team’s regular long snapper could put him in an unfamiliar position on game day.Dave Toub has a backup plan for Travis Kelce at long snapperToub recently explained why he wants Kelce ready to handle long-snapping duties if an emergency strikes. Speaking to reporters about the Chiefs’ backup options, the special teams coordinator said, “I definitely thought about it, and I said to myself, ‘We need to get Kelce.’”He added, “Because Kelce’s our guy. You can dial him up in two snaps, and he’s ready to go, but we need to practice it. The other guy that does it now is Gray, Noah Gray. So, two really good athletes that fit the bill.”The comments highlight Kansas City’s plan to prepare more than one player for a position that often goes unnoticed until something goes wrong. Long snappers handle the precise snaps required for punts and field goals. A poor snap can disrupt the entire play, leaving the holder, kicker and coverage unit scrambling to recover.The Chiefs currently rely on James Winchester as their regular long snapper. He has played every Kansas City game since joining the team in 2015, building a streak of 205 appearances, including playoff games, as of January 2026. The Chiefs re-signed him to a one-year, $1.75 million contract in March 2026. Chiefs have already faced a long-snapper emergencyKansas City has a reason to take this backup plan seriously. During a preseason game against the Detroit Lions in August 2024, Winchester left with a shoulder injury. Noah Gray stepped in to snap for punter Matt Araiza on Harrison Butker’s 56-yard field goal.Gray, a tight end, had never long-snapped in a game at any level. Kelce could not take over because he had already finished his day after the second offensive possession. Toub later praised Kelce’s ability and identified him as another backup option.The Chiefs’ concerns also echo a problem Jacksonville faced on October 12, 2026, against the Philadelphia Eagles. Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik injured his shoulder in the first quarter, forcing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton to take over. A high snap disrupted the timing on a late missed extra point, although Hamilton later snapped for Cam Little’s 57-yard game-winning field goal in Jacksonville’s 19-17 victory.That sequence showed how quickly a long-snapper injury can affect a game. Toub wants Kansas City’s emergency options to get practice before a similar situation arises.Kelce has already produced 246 receiving yards and two touchdowns through four games in the 2026 season, according to the supplied report. He finished 2025 with 76 catches for 851 yards.As of now, the Chiefs do not need Kelce to replace Winchester. But Toub wants him prepared if the situation changes. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Jauan Jennings & Top Landing Spots Ahead of Deadline
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. and Minnesota Vikings' Jauan Jennings are reportedly becoming trade targets for wideout-needy teams in the wake of Marvin Harrison Jr.'s move to the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. and Minnesota Vikings' Jauan Jennings are reportedly becoming trade targets for wideout-needy teams in the wake of Marvin Harrison Jr.'s move to the Houston Texans.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday Thomas' name "continues to come up in conversations around the league as Parker Washington solidifies himself as the Jags' top wideout."

Jones speculated the Texans' willingness to give up a 2027 second-round pick for Harrison could help increase Thomas' trade price, but predicted the Jaguars won't be "in a rush" to trade the wide receiver.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported the same day on his Substack Jennings has "been the subject of trade speculation."

Pelissero predicted Jennings will nonetheless remain with the Vikings because "the team still believes Jennings can help it and Jennings wants to be in Minnesota."

The Jaguars (4-1) and Vikings (5-0) have until the Nov. 10 trade deadline to bolster their lineups for potential playoff runs this winter.

Thomas, like Harrison, is a former first-round pick who has seen his usage drop during the early stretch of the season. He has made just nine catches on 18 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown through five games of his third season with the Jaguars.

He most recently recorded no catches on three targets in the Jags' Week 5 win last Sunday over the Philadelphia Eagles.

The majority of Trevor Lawrence's targets have gone this season to Parker Washington, who is breaking out in the final season of his rookie contract with 22 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns.

NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported in September the Jaguars and Washington had discussed an extension in the range of three years and $75 million but were "unlikely" to finalize a deal ahead of the season.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported earlier this week he would not "be surprised if those discussions pick up again during the season."

The Jaguars reaching an extension with Washington could lock him in as the team's top wideout going forward and potentially increase the chances general manager James Gladstone would be willing to deal Thomas by the deadline.

Jennings has made just two catches for nine yards in four games despite being on the field for 201 offensive snaps since signing a one-year deal with the Vikings this offseason. ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport recently speculated a return to the San Francisco 49ers would make sense for Jennings given the team's injury loss of Deebo Samuel.

Whether Jennings sees more usage in the Vikings' pass attack over the team's three games between now and the trade deadline could impact whether the veteran wideout ultimately lands on the trade block.

articles.title: Myles Garrett's Outfit Caused NFL to Call Rams, New Rumors Surface on Warning and Potential Fine
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett received a warning from the NFL regarding the outfit he wore on the sideline of Monday night's overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett received a warning from the NFL regarding the outfit he wore on the sideline of Monday night's overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones .

Garrett, who was placed on injured reserve after undergoing knee surgery ahead of Week 2, wore a tracksuit not branded with the Rams logo or colors on the sideline of the Week 5 matchup.

Players are expected to wear team-issued gear on the sidelines, Jones noted. The Rams "heard from the league office about it," although Garrett did not receive a fine, according to Jones.

Jones described the warning as part of the NFL's "warn first, fine later" policy.

The news comes a week and a half after the NFL announced relaxed celebration rules and stated players will be warned first before receiving fines for "gray area" violations.

Jones noted the NFL might be "offering a small olive branch to players" after recently rescinding fines issues to multiple players, including for "gray area" celebrations from Ja'Marr Chase and Jameson Williams.

The NFL also walked back the league's previous policy to fine players who imitate drinking in on-field celebrations by rescinding fines to Kyle Juszcyzyk and Jake Ferguson.

The league rulebook states potential fines of $11,941 for a first offense of "unauthorized logo/branding or intellectual property," as well as a $5,971 penalty for "uniform violations."

Garrett's potential rule violation involved a Jumpman tracksuit, Jones noted. That follows Jordan Brand's January announcement Garrett has signed a new deal with the company after setting the NFL's single-season sacks record in his final season with the Cleveland Browns.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September. He has yet to return to practice this week as Rams (2-3) prepare for a Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals (1-4).

When asked Friday if the Rams intend to open Garrett's 21-day window to return by bringing him back to practice next week, head coach Sean McVay said he would provide an update Monday.

"There's benchmarks that you want to hit in the midst of this rehab and recovery. He's hitting all those... I'd love to have him back out there, but not at the expense of rushing him back," McVay said about Garrett.

It sounds like Garrett could be wearing blue and yellow on the sidelines until he is able to return.

articles.title: College Football Playoff expansion is just the latest example of why 'growing the game' isn't always healthy
articles.summary: The college football playoff expansion to 24 teams takes "grow the game" too far, raising the question: if 12 wasn't enough, where does it end?
articles.body: "Grow the game." It's a phrase you hear quite often on social media these days, particularly with more "niche" sports like hockey or golf. Just this past week, a different sport has made yet another attempt to "grow the game," as college football announced it will be expanding its playoff from 12 to 24 teams sometime in the near future. Plenty has been written on why this is a bad idea, mostly with regard to destroying what was once the greatest and most consequential regular season in sports, and while I share those sentiments, I'm looking to attack this from a different angle. This isn't even the first time college football has attempted to "grow the game" and appeal to a wider audience. HERE'S WHY THE COACHES ASSOCIATION'S 24-TEAM COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF COULD RUIN THE SPORT The College Football Playoff, since its very inception, was created in part to appease those who cried that the BCS was an unfair and antiquated system. So we went to a four-game model, then a 12-game model, and now that 12 isn't enough, we have moved to 24. CFP, NCAA TOURNAMENT EXPANSION BOTH DRAW BACKLASH, BUT ONE IS DEFINITIVELY WORSE THAN THE OTHER Surely, that's the end of it, right? If 24 is good, is 32 better? Where is the limiting principle? And it's not just the Playoff, either. Conference expansion and realignment, as well as an unfettered transfer portal, has college football looking more and more like the NFL by the day, and that's by design. SEC, BIG TEN ARE DOMINATING COLLEGE FOOTBALL THANKS TO MASSIVE ADVANTAGES OVER OTHER CONFERENCES One of the biggest arguments I've seen in favor of the expanded CFP is that the NFL has a certain percentage of its teams make the postseason, and that a 24-team model will have those numbers look closer to the NFL. With all due respect, if I wanted to watch the NFL, I'd just watch the NFL. HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL Can we stop trying to turn college football into something that "everyone" wants to watch? Because you're not just appealing to a wider audience, you're appealing to a lowest common denominator as a result. Fans were insanely passionate and regionally focused, and the game reflected that. The folks who "didn't get it" were more than welcome to tune out. I understand from a money perspective why college football is trying to "grow the game," and my colleague Trey Wallace wrote a great piece about that, but sacrificing the will of loyal fans for the almighty dollar is unhealthy for the sport long term. I mentioned the NHL trying to "grow the game," and while that has gotten them slightly more exposure, it's also attracted fans who read "Heated Rivalry" with pronouns and "Free Palestine" in their social media bio. articles.title: Donovan McNabb Reacts to Jayden Daniels, Commanders' Tie After Famously Not Knowing NFL Rule
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles legend Donovan McNabb had sympathy for Jayden Daniels after the Washington Commanders' late-game blunder last week resulted in a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles legend Donovan McNabb had sympathy for Jayden Daniels after the Washington Commanders' late-game blunder last week resulted in a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants.

Speaking to The Athletic's Rustin Dodd , McNabb described the "deflated" feeling that comes with the scrutiny of a high-profile mistake like what Daniels experienced:

"You feel deflated; you just feel deflated. But still, you know you've got a job to do, because no matter what people on the outside are saying or what's going on, it doesn't control the path you set for yourself.My safe haven was: We all go through adversity. But it's all on who's able to overcome that and be able to move forward positively.

"Being a quarterback and understanding the highs and lows of the position, I was able to refocus and move on. Now, obviously, being in Philadelphia, that conversation went on week after week — no matter if we were winning or not — because they would always go back to that game and wonder if that would haunt us going forward to whatever seed we were or home-field advantage. I also wasn't the only one who said that. But that's the thing: the quarterback is supposed to know the rules."

McNabb is familiar with the experience because he infamously said he "never even knew" ties were a thing in the NFL after a 2008 game between the Eagles and Cincinnati Bengals ended with a 13-13 score.

"I've never been a part of a tie. I never even knew that was in the rule book," McNabb said at the time. "It's part of the rules, and we have to go with it. I was looking forward to getting the opportunity to get out there and try to drive to win the game. But unfortunately, with the rules, we settled with a tie."

Daniels had the Commanders in field-goal range late in the overtime period against the Giants, but decided to snap the ball and run around to take a sack when they didn't have any timeouts remaining.

The explanation from Daniels after the game was everyone on the team has to be better at communicating.

"We've just got to communicate that, that's the whole thing," Daniels said. "It starts with me, communicating to the whole offense in the huddle. And I think everybody will say that from the top down."

McNabb told Dodd that from his perspective it "just seemed like they were out of whack" without knowing the situation and no one trying to communicate:

"No one knew what the situation was. Even if you look across the board, the offensive line didn't. Receivers were kind of jogging back. The timing of everything just looked bad. They were in the huddle with 50-something seconds left. Quarterbacks always get a lot of the criticism. And in that situation, it's shared between quarterback, head coach and (offensive) coordinator."

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said the blunder falls on him because he needed to make sure Daniels knew to either spike the ball or throw it out of bounds.

Even though McNabb caught flack for not knowing ties were a thing, it did help that the Eagles never really came all that close to winning in overtime. They didn't run a play in Cincinnati territory during the extra period.

The Bengals missed a 47-yard field goal with seven seconds remaining. McNabb got one last pass attempt off from his own 37-yard line that landed incomplete as time expired.

Daniels had Washington in position to at least get a try for a game-winning field goal before taking the final snap.

"I mean, Michael Jordan missed however many shots that could have won games," McNabb told Dodd. "You think he harps on that? No, he takes the next shot when it comes about. We learn life lessons in sports about work ethic, passion, determination and if you're goal-oriented. How do you assert yourself each day? You have to do that if you're working a 9-to-5. These are lessons that I teach my kids."

Interestingly, two of the last three NFL games that ended in a tie were between the Commanders and Giants. They previously played to a 20-20 result in Week 13 of the 2022 season.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Drops Honest Quote on Todd Monken Trash Talk Ahead of Ravens vs. Browns Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry is expecting some extra trash talk in the Cleveland locker room now that his former offensive coordinator Todd Monken is coaching the Browns.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry is expecting some extra trash talk in the Cleveland locker room now that his former offensive coordinator Todd Monken is coaching the Browns.

"He might not say it in the media, but to the team, he definitely talks a lot of trash and letting them know he wants to beat us," Henry said Thursday ahead of Sunday's game between the Ravens and Browns in Cleveland.

Monken said Friday he had been sent the clip of Henry mentioning his trash talk by multiple people ahead of the Week 6 matchup (h/t ESPN's Justin Cooper).

"It's not personal. It's strictly business... do I want to win? Not more than any other week," Monken said. "And my message isn't any different this week than it was the previous five weeks."

Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey didn't seem to expect Monken would approaching the matchup like any other game when asked about his former coordinator earlier this week.

"If I know Todd the way I think I know Todd, he will want to kick our tail," Humphrey said (h/t The Baltimore Sun 's Josh Tolentino).

Monken served as offensive coordinator under former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh from 2023 to 2025, a span over which multiple key players including Lamar Jackson and Rashod Bateman recorded the best seasons of their NFL careers so far.

Bateman said earlier this week it would be up to Ravens players to shift the narrative away from the matchup against their former coordinator (h/t Fox Baltimore's Morgan Adsit ).

"I think, when you're a player, you've got to make the choice whether you want to make this game about Todd Monken, or do you want to make it about going to play football," Bateman said. "I'm pretty sure Todd Monken is not worried about Rashod Bateman, or what he's doing in Baltimore. He's worried about getting the Cleveland Browns right to beat us."

The Ravens (4-1-0) are heading into the matchup on a three-game win streak but without Jackson, who was ruled out for Week 6 with an ankle injury.

Tyler Huntley will be starting in Jackson's place against Deshaun Watson and the Browns (3-2), which are looking to bounce back from a Week 5 loss at the New York Jets. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET in Cleveland.

articles.title: JJ Jansen Makes NFL History As Panthers Long Snapper Sets Record
articles.summary: JJ Jansen will play his 282nd game, breaking the all-time record for long snappers. See why this 40-year-old veteran is a true legend.
articles.body:
History is being made this Sunday, and it is not about touchdowns or interceptions. JJ Jansen will take the field against the Philadelphia Eagles to play his 282nd career game, a number that no other long snapper in NFL history has ever reached. While most fans forget the specialist who snaps the ball between his legs, Jansen has turned a tiny job into a massive legacy. He is not just playing; he is proving that consistency beats flash every single time.

Per NBC Sports , this milestone breaks a tie with Trey Junkin, the man Jansen watched as a kid in Arizona. The 40-year-old has spent his entire regular-season career with the Panthers, a rarity in a league where players jump ship for every extra dollar. He started in 2009 after a trade, and he has been the anchor ever since. This is not luck. It is a skill set so rare that only a handful of men in the world can do it at this level.

Jansen did not learn this craft in a fancy camp or a high-tech facility. He learned it from his dad on a patch of grass in their backyard. The technique required for snapping a football is so precise that a bad snap can cost a team a field goal. Jansen told Darin Gantt of Panthers.com, "I still remember we practiced in the same way every single time," recalling the hours they spent in front of a tree. He stood at one end, and his dad stood 15 yards away. They had good nights and bad nights, but they kept going. That grind built a player who refuses to quit.

Former kicker John Kasay, who held the Panthers' games played record before Jansen, sees something special in this work ethic. "I think he never got bored with it," Kasay said. The job is repetitive, but Jansen treats every snap like it matters. He has played 281 games for Carolina alone, and he is still going strong. If he plays every game this season, he will finish with 294 games, placing him 18th on the all-time list for any player. That is a testament to a player who never lost his edge.

Long snappers do not get the glory, but they get the job done. Jansen knows that the only stat that matters for his position is games played. As long as you do not mess up, you keep your spot. He has done that for 17 years. He once joked about watching Junkin warm up on first down, thinking the Cardinals were so bad that the special teams guys had to be ready early. "I always thought it was really funny that the punter and the long snapper would warm up on first down because back then the Cardinals were terrible," Jansen said. Now, he is the one setting the standard that others will chase for decades.

With the next game set for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the Eagles, Jansen is ready to add another chapter to his story. He is showing no signs of slowing down, even as he passes the 40-year mark. This is what loyalty looks like in the NFL. He is not just a player; he is a record holder who earned every single one of his snaps. Keep pounding, JJ.

articles.title: Jaguars make Brian Thomas Jr. decision amid league-wide trade interest
articles.summary: This trade decision from the Jaguars shouldn't come as a surprise.
articles.body:
As the NFL trade deadline nears, there is a ton of interest on the Jacksonville Jaguars , but it's not about the 4-1 team being buyers, but rather about if one player is going to be made available.

Through the first five weeks of the season, Brian Thomas Jr.'s role in the offense has been minimal at best. With Parker Washington breaking out and Jakobi Meyers signed to an extension, Thomas's name has popped up in trade rumors.

However, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Jaguars have made a decision on whether Thomas will be available for trade or not. Unsurprisingly, as of Week 6, Thomas is not on the trade block despite league-wide interest.

Jaguars don't put Brian Thomas Jr. on trade block despite interest

"After the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, league eyes have turned to Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr.," Jones reports. "... But Jacksonville does not have him on the trade block."

While there might be interest from NFL clubs about a trade for Thomas, it appears that the Jaguars are not making him available right now.

Washington, Meyers, and Josh Cameron are involved in this Jaguars' passing attack, and Thomas has fallen by the wayside after being taken in the first round in 2024.

But, despite being an obvious trade candidate, the Jaguars are Super Bowl contenders this season, and Jones' report indicates they have no intention of trading Thomas this season.

His field-stretching ability and upside as a receiver are enough to justify keeping him on the team, even if his overall involvement in the offense is minimal.

He's not on the trade block right now, so fans or NFL teams hoping for their team to improve their WR room might have to look for other WR trade targets this Fall instead of Thomas.

articles.title: KC Chiefs Potential Cost in Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Gets Big Week 6 Update in New Report
articles.summary: A new report sheds new light on what it might cost the Kansas City Chiefs to make a trade for […]
articles.body:
A new report sheds new light on what it might cost the Kansas City Chiefs to make a trade for one-time Pro Bowler Brian Thomas Jr., and it is a price they are probably unwilling to meet.

Following a frustrating 6-11 finish last season, the Chiefs are back to being the cream of the crop in the AFC after the first five weeks of the 2026 season. Heading into their game against the Los Angeles Chargers on the Week 6 NFL schedule , Kansas City is one of the last undefeated teams left in the league.

Their defense has been rock solid, and their run game — led by early MVP contender Kenneth Walker III — has been fantastic. However, they could use more weapons in their passing attack. Especially after Tyquan Thornton suffered a likely season-ending ankle injury in Week 4 and with Rashee Rice battling knee and hamstring issues.

For weeks, the team has been linked to several moves for a receiver. One player recently connected to the Chiefs was Marvin Harrison Jr. However, last week, the Arizona Cardinals shipped the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft to the Houston Texans to reunite him with his QB at Ohio State , CJ Stroud.

With Harrison Jr. off the board, KC has also been connected to another junior in trade speculation, and that is the Jacksonville Jaguars . After looking like a new long-term star when he posted 87 catches, 1,282 yards, and made the Pro Bowl in his rookie season, he has completely fallen out of favor with head coach Liam Coen over the last two years.

After five games, Thomas Jr. has just 9 catches for 105 yards. The Jags continue to suggest publicly that they have no interest in trading him. However, it seems like they are just holding on to him in case of injury. If the 4-1 team with one of the best defenses in the NFL can improve their roster for a title run, it would be silly not to start taking trade offers on the former LSU star.

Brian Thomas Jr. trade could cost the Kansas City Chiefs a first-round pick

So, if they did start taking calls and the Chiefs reached out, what might the price be? Well, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones, " Harrison Jr. going for a 2027 second-round pick helps the Jaguars only if they do wind up dealing him ."

Thomas Jr. has had a far better three-year career than Harrison Jr. The Jaguars receiver has 36 more catches, 516 more yards, and the same number of receiving touchdowns as the player who went 19 spots ahead of him in the 2024 NFL Draft. It means he will come at a higher price, and that could be the Chiefs having to give up a first-round pick — which is something Arizona was reportedly looking for — or maybe two second-rounders.

If this were the Los Angeles Rams , that team might be willing to fork over such valuable picks because they are betting on Thomas Jr.'s potential to be a Pro Bowl-level player for years to come. However, the Chiefs have never been a franchise to risk valuable draft assets in trades. They actually move players for picks before they know they will lose them in free agency for nothing.

articles.title: While Patrick Mahomes rules the NFL, Brittany Mahomes Is building her own women’s soccer legacy with the Kansas City current’s $140 million stadium
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has spent years making a name for himself in the NFL, winning Super Bowls and becoming one of the most recognised quarterbacks in American
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has spent years making a name for himself in the NFL, winning Super Bowls and becoming one of the most recognised quarterbacks in American football. But while his career with the Kansas City Chiefs often puts the family in the headlines, Brittany Mahomes has been working on something of her own. She is a co-owner of the Kansas City Current, a professional women’s soccer team that is helping bring more attention to women’s sports. Her journey from playing soccer to owning a club shows that her story is about much more than being married to an NFL star. She has her own sporting background, business interests and a role in shaping the future of women’s soccer.How did Brittany Mahomes go from playing soccer to owning a professional team?Long before Brittany became known to NFL fans, soccer was already a big part of her life. She played the sport at the University of Texas at Tyler, where she earned a degree in kinesiology. She later played professional soccer in Iceland for a year before turning her attention to fitness and business.Her experience as a player gave her a closer look at the demands of competitive sport and the work athletes put in behind the scenes. After leaving professional soccer, she launched an online fitness training business in 2019, giving her another way to stay connected to sports and help people work towards their fitness goals.Her move into team ownership came in December 2020, when Brittany joined Angie and Chris Long in bringing a new National Women’s Soccer League team to Kansas City. The club was first known as Kansas City NWSL before taking the name Kansas City Current in 2021.This was an important step in her career because she was no longer involved in sports only as a player. She now had a role in building a club, helping it grow and giving women’s soccer a stronger place in the city. Patrick Mahomes joined the ownership group in 2023, but Brittany had been part of the project from its early days.What has Brittany Mahomes done for the Kansas City current?Owning a professional sports team involves much more than attending matches and supporting players from the stands. It means helping build a club that can attract fans, find business partners, provide the right facilities and compete at a high level.Brittany is part of the ownership group behind the Kansas City Current, which has invested in its players, training facilities and wider presence in the community. The aim has been to build a club where women’s soccer receives serious attention and the athletes have the resources they need to perform.One of the clearest signs of that ambition came in 2021, when the owners announced plans for a new stadium. The project gave the Current a chance to create a permanent home designed specifically for women’s professional soccer rather than having to share a venue built for another team.The club’s progress has also been visible on the pitch. In 2024, the Current scored 57 regular-season goals and recorded 16 wins. A year later, they won the 2025 NWSL Shield after finishing the regular season with the league’s best record. The award was the first in the club’s history.These results cannot be credited to one owner alone. Players, coaches, staff and the entire ownership group have played their parts. Still, the team’s growth shows why Brittany’s involvement is worth covering as a sports story in its own right.Why Is CPKC Stadium such an important part of Brittany Mahomes’ work?When CPKC Stadium opened in March 2024, it gave the Kansas City Current something few professional women’s teams had ever had: a stadium built specifically for a women’s professional sports team.Located along Kansas City’s riverfront, the venue has a capacity of around 11,500 and was privately funded by the club’s ownership group. It hosted its first match on March 16, 2024, when the Current beat the Portland Thorns 5-4 in front of a sold-out crowd.The stadium matters because facilities affect how athletes train, compete and prepare for games. A dedicated venue also gives a team greater control over its matchday experience, ticket sales, events and relationships with fans.For Brittany, the project connects her background as a soccer player with her work as an owner. She knows the sport from the playing side, but she is now also part of a group investing in the places and resources that help professional athletes do their jobs.The stadium also sends a wider message about women’s sports. Female athletes deserve proper facilities, strong support and the chance to play in front of large crowds. Building a venue around a women’s team makes that commitment visible, rather than leaving it as something owners simply promise.How is Brittany Mahomes creating her own identity beyond Patrick Mahomes?Being married to one of the NFL’s biggest stars naturally brings public attention. Patrick’s achievements with the Chiefs have made the Mahomes family familiar to football fans, but Brittany’s work with the Current gives her a separate role in professional sports.She has a playing background, experience in fitness entrepreneurship and a stake in a growing soccer club. These are parts of her career that exist beyond her relationship with Patrick, even though their public profiles often overlap.Their shared involvement in the Kansas City Current also shows how their interests have moved beyond football. Patrick built his career on the NFL field, while Brittany has helped develop a club in a different sport. Together, they are part of a project that connects professional sports, business and the Kansas City community.Brittany’s work does not mean she is responsible for every success the Current achieves, nor does her ownership alone solve the challenges facing women’s soccer. But her involvement gives her a direct role in a club that has invested in its players and facilities and has already enjoyed success in the NWSL.Patrick Mahomes will remain known for what he achieves with the Chiefs.
