articles.title: Patriots activate WR A.J. Brown from IR after 4-game absence
articles.summary: Brown has been sidelined since suffering a high-ankle sprain during New England's season opener.
articles.body:
Receiver A.J. Brown will play in the New England Patriots' Week 6 matchup with the New York Jets after the team announced on Saturday it had activated him from injured reserve .

Brown, 29, has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots' season opener versus the Seattle Seahawks. He left New England's 13-10 loss in the third quarter after catching three passes for 26 yards, and was placed on injured reserve the next day.

Going on IR meant that Brown would have to sit out for the next four games. Thus, he was eligible to be activated this week. Brown was a limited participant in all three of the Patriots' practice sessions for the week and is listed as questionable for Sunday .

Earlier in the week, head coach Mike Vrabel said "there is a chance" the veteran receiver would be able to return for Week 6.

"Whenever he'll be back, he should help us," Vrabel said on Monday during his weekly appearance on Boston's WEEI. "I hope that he's going to help us, but that remains to be seen yet when he'll be back. So we'll see how he does and move from there."

Brown's return looked like a strong possibility when the Patriots placed receiver Mack Hollins on IR prior to Week 5's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Before going on IR, Hollins had the most catches among Patriots wide receivers with 15 for 209 yards. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson and tight end Hunter Henry also have 15 receptions for New England (3-2).

The Patriots acquired Brown during the offseason from the Philadelphia Eagles, in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth-round selection. Though he had 1,003 receiving yards last season with the Eagles (his lowest total in four seasons), Brown had reportedly grown frustrated with quarterback Jalen Hurts — and the Eagles' offense in general.

That led to Brown being traded before a three-year, $96 million extension kicked in that takes him through the 2029 season.

Brown is in his eighth NFL season, which began with the Tennessee Titans for three years. He was the team's second-round selection (No. 51 overall) out of Ole Miss.

The 6-foot-1 receiver was dealt to the Eagles during the 2022 NFL Draft for first- and fourth-round picks. He subsequently received a four-year, $100 million extension from Philadelphia.

A three-time Pro Bowler and two-time Second-Team All-Pro selection, Brown has 527 career receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns.

articles.title: Eagles place QB Jalen Hurts on IR with blood clot as team changes course
articles.summary: Hurts will miss at least the next four weeks for the Eagles.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have changed their minds after consulting with a number of doctors and medical experts and will be placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after a superficial blood clot was discovered in his leg .

According to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , while the Eagles initially did not plan to put Hurts on IR, the information they received has led them to decide to shut him down indefinitely.

Hurts has already been ruled out for this week's game against the Carolina Panthers. Once he is placed on IR, he will be out for at least four weeks.

The Eagles released a statement Thursday saying that Hurts asked the team's training staff to treat his calf on Oct. 8 after being cleated during a game against the Los Angeles Rams days earlier. An ultrasound was performed on Oct. 10 after the team flew to London. The results showed a superficial blood clot, but doctors and medical staff concluded "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play."

The team says Hurts, who did not carry an injury designation before the game, played "without limitation" last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars and was able to practice fully Wednesday after receiving treatment earlier in the week.

A follow-up ultrasound was done Wednesday which "revealed movement in the small blood clot."

Hurts will miss Week 6 and there is currently no timetable for a return. The Eagles said they have been in communication with the NFL regarding the matter.

Tanner McKee, who has played six career NFL games since being drafted in 2023, will be the Eagles' starter.

articles.title: Bradley Chubb Fined for Taunting in Exchange That Led to Alaric Jackson Punch After Bills-Rams
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb has been fined $14,329 for taunting Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson after Buffalo's 37-34 road win over L.A. last Monday.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb has been fined $14,329 for taunting Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson after Buffalo's 37-34 road win over L.A. last Monday.

Chubb's remarks led to Jackson throwing a punch, and the NFL initially suspended the Ram for two games before reducing it down to one after an appeal.

Chubb told his side of the story to reporters on Wednesday.

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb began. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

ESPN's Sarah Barshop reported that Jackson and Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker were exchanging jerseys on the field before Chubb approached with some comments. Jackson punched Chubb after the remarks.

Chubb is in his eighth NFL season. The two-time Pro Bowler has played for the Denver Broncos, Miami Dolphins and Bills. He's made five starts in his first season for Buffalo, amassing 17 tackles, seven quarterback hits and 1.5 sacks.

Chubb and the first-place Bills will visit the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Bears-Falcons, Severity of Hamstring Tear
articles.summary: Caleb Williams is expected to start against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams is expected to start against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Williams previously said that he doesn't know if he would be on the field for Sunday's game.

"Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return.

Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season.

And while he seems to be ready to return, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious."

Williams' status has been the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears.

He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable."

"He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there."

Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league."

Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets.

However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers.

Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions.

Now, it appears Williams will be back on the field this week.

articles.title: Eagles' Jeremiah Trotter, Jaguars' Bryan Thomas Jr. Fined by NFL for Fight That Led to Ejections
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. both received fines for their involvement in a fight that occurred during a Week 5 matchup between the two teams.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. both received fines for their involvement in a fight that occurred during a Week 5 matchup between the two teams.

Trotter was fined $6,428 by the NFL while Thomas was fined $4,972, per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.

The scuffle started as both players became tangled up during the opening kickoff of the game before the physical altercation continued after the play was over. Trotter and Thomas were both ejected from the contest.

The Jaguars ultimately won by the final score of 19-17.

Referee Ron Torbert explained the decision to eject both players after the game.

"They were disqualified for continuous non-football actions after the play was over," Torbert told Mark Long of the Associated Press (h/t Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk).

Trotter has been a key depth piece for the Eagles since he was selected by the team with a fifth-round pick in the 2024 NFL draft. He was set to replace Jihaad Campbell in Philadelphia's starting defense against Jacksonville prior to his ejection.

In five games this season, Trotter has amassed 19 tackles and one pass defended.

As for Thomas, he's an undrafted rookie who has served as a rotational option on the Jaguars' defensive line.

The 22-year-old has recorded one tackle and one quarterback hit in four appearances to open his NFL career.

Jacksonville was able to emerge victorious over Philadelphia despite facing a three-point deficit with eight seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, returning a kickoff for 53 yards to set up a game-winning field goal with one second left.

The Jaguars improved to 4-1, while the Eagles fell to 2-3.

articles.title: 'Get S--t Together,' Gayle Benson's Surprising Quote on Saints, Loomis Draws Reaction from NFL Execs
articles.summary: People around the NFL were surprised with New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson's willingness to bluntly express frustration with her team's 1-4 start to the season, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday.
articles.body:
People around the NFL were surprised with New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson's willingness to bluntly express frustration with her team's 1-4 start to the season, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday.

Benson directly called out head coach Kellen Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis while describing the Saints' record as "not acceptable" during an eight-minute speech at a Tuesday luncheon, according to NOLA.com's Rod Walker and Matthew Paras .

According to Jones, the mention of Loomis especially "caught the attention of many around the league."

"Loomis is seen as, essentially, a lifetime appointee to the Saints GM position... Loomis is in his 25th year as GM, longer than anyone else with GM in his title not named Jerry Jones," Jones noted.

According to Jones, one Saints source said about Benson's comments, "It obviously means get s--t together."

Benson said in her speech she saw Kellen Moore and his staff as "responsible for preparing out players to perform," per Walker and Paras.

"Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success," Benson continued, per Walker and Paras. "Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."

Jones reported Saturday that "folks I talk to don't remember Benson ever being so pointed."

Benson attended Saints practice on Friday. The two could be seen embracing on the sideline in a video shared by Locked On Saints' Ross Jackson.

"It's always good to see Mrs. B. She likes to pop in and catch some practice here and there... she's always supportive," Moore told reporters Friday.

When asked if Benson had addressed her comments, Moore said, "We talked throughout the week, and so we're all good... we're all just trying to reach the same goal. We all want to win football games, and so we're all working towards that."

The Saints have recorded just one winning campaign and no playoff appearances since Sean Payton stepped down ahead of the 2022 season. Only six teams have won fewer games than the Saints over that span, per StatMuse .

Benson has previously backed Loomis during this stretch. She told The Times-Picayune 's Jeff Duncan after a 2-8 start to the 2025 season it was "ridiculous" to consider firing the Saints' longtime general manager.

Moore will get his next chance to turn the 2026 season around and potentially take some heat off Loomis when the Saints return to action with a Sunday road game against Jameis Winston and the New York Giants.

articles.title: Do Steelers have enough at WR with Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson out?
articles.summary: Coach Mike McCarthy will also want to see more from the star pass rushing trio of T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig.
articles.body:
Fresh off their most complete victory of the season against the Indianapolis Colts , the Pittsburgh Steelers will travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an NFL Week 6 matchup Oct. 18.

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers will look to continue a streak of three consecutive games with at least three touchdown passes. Running back Jaylen Warren will serve as the hot hand of his supporting cast, having climbed to No. 3 in the NFL in scrimmage yards over the past three games.

Injuries, however, will loom as a problem that coach Mike McCarthy's team must solve for if it hopes to improve to 4-2 and keep pace in a strong AFC North division.

Here is USA TODAY's list of things to watch for from a Pittsburgh perspective.

Does this team have enough left at receiver?

Michael Pittman Jr. was the prize offseason addition via a trade with the Colts but hit injured reserve last week with a stubborn foot injury. Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek were subsequently injured against the Colts and have been ruled out for Week 6 by McCarthy. That leaves top target DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard and fringe NFL talent beyond them. Rookie Kaden Wetjen is technically a receiver but made the roster almost exclusively for his kick return abilities coming out of training camp and the preseason. Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson are practice squad guys with 26 NFL receptions between them. One of them will likely need to step up to draw at least some heat away from the top two options. Otherwise, it could be a difficult day for the passing game.

How have Pittsburgh Steelers head coaches fared through the years?

The Steelers registered just two quarterback hits and one sack in the win against the Colts, per Pro Football Focus data. That lack of pressure gave Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones the time to make throws that kept his team in the game before his effectiveness began to wane late as the offense became one-dimensional. Star linebacker T.J. Watt has just one sack in the past three games after starting the season with 3.5 in the first two games. Running mate Alex Highsmith has no sacks over the same span. He had two in the first pair of games. Veteran Nick Herbig is still sitting on zero for the season after inking a $100-million contract extension in the offseason. The Steelers will want to see more from those guys to help a secondary that's struggling with the loss of cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to a trade and injuries of varying degrees to veterans Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean.

The signing of veteran Elandon Roberts to the practice squad this week raised some eyebrows for DC Patrick Graham's defense. This will be his third stint with the Steelers overall and second this year after he was cut from the initial 53-man roster in September. He previously manned the inside under former coach Mike Tomlin in 2023 and 2024 before joining Graham last season in Las Vegas. It could just be a depth move, but trade rumors swirled around starter Patrick Queen in the offseason, with some tying him to the same Dallas team that has already completed deals with the Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. and Broderick Jones. The NFL trade deadline looms on Nov. 10, so eyes will be on Queen to see if he could be on the move – and if Roberts is on the roster now as a known quantity of an insurance policy.

Is the running game's momentum for real?

Over the past two games, running back Jaylen Warren has rushed for 194 yards and averaged six yards per carry. Whether or not the injured Rico Dowdle re-joins him in the backfield this week, a third consecutive solid performance would allay a lot of concerns that crept out of the first two games, when the Steelers totaled just 149 yards and averaged 3.38 yards per carry. Especially because the passing game figures to be quite shorthanded with the trio of receivers out. Continue to keep an eye on the revamped right side of the offensive line of guard Brock Hoffman and rookie tackle Max Iheanachor for continued growth.

articles.title: Former Broncos GM John Beake, architect of back-to-back Super Bowl champions, dies at 87
articles.summary: Beake worked for the Broncos in some form from 1979 to 2000.
articles.body:
John Beake, the former Denver Broncos general manager who helped build back-to-back Super Bowl championships in 1998 and 1999, has died, the franchise announced Saturday . He was 87 years old.

Beake served as Broncos GM from 1985 until 1999, but worked for the team with different titles before and after that tenure. The Penn State graduate first joined the organization as director of pro personnel in 1979 and worked his way up to GM, then took on a new role as vice president of administration after the 1998-99 season.

"The Broncos are saddened by the passing of longtime executive John Beake, who made an enduring impact on our organization during more than two decades with the team. John helped guide the Broncos to five Super Bowl appearances, including back-to-back World Championships, and was a respected leader throughout one of the most successful eras in franchise history. "Following his time in Denver, he remained an influential figure through his work with the NFL and on the Broncos Ring of Fame Committee. Our deepest condolences are with his wife, Marcia, his sons, Chip and Chris, and the entire Beake family."

"The Broncos are saddened by the passing of longtime executive John Beake, who made an enduring impact on our organization during more than two decades with the team. John helped guide the Broncos to five Super Bowl appearances, including back-to-back World Championships, and was a respected leader throughout one of the most successful eras in franchise history.

"Following his time in Denver, he remained an influential figure through his work with the NFL and on the Broncos Ring of Fame Committee. Our deepest condolences are with his wife, Marcia, his sons, Chip and Chris, and the entire Beake family."

It was in 1983, during Beake's time as the director of player personnel, that he was in the room for the trade that would define the Broncos' next two decades, landing No. 1 overall draft pick John Elway from the Baltimore Colts. Beake downplayed his role in the negotiations, calling himself " a support person ."

Two years later, Beake took over the Broncos front office following the resignation of then-general manager Hein Poulus. Under head coach Dan Reeves, the Broncos proceeded to reach the Super Bowl three times in four years, losing each time.

Reeves was fired in 1992 and was replaced by Wade Phillips, who was succeeded two years later by Mike Shanahan. That hire worked out well.

After his time with the Broncos, Beake took on an executive role with the ill-fated NFL Europe until his retirement in 2004. He remained connected to the Broncos organization in retirement.

Before landing in Denver, Beake served as an offensive backfield coach for the Kansas City Chiefs and New Orleans Saints. In total, he worked in some sort of NFL role for 35 years, interrupted only by a single-season stint as offensive coordinator at Colorado State.

articles.title: ‘NFL Is a Nepo Baby System’ — Ex-Chargers DT Raises Serious Concerns Over Arch Manning’s NFL Draft Stock

articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning entered the 2026 season with plenty of hype as a potential top pick in next year's NFL Draft. However, his inconsistent performances have raised questions about his draft stock.

A former Chargers DT even took to X to voice his disappointment, delivering some harsh criticism of the 22-year-old's performance.

Breiden Fehoko Raises Red Flags Over Arch Manning's NFL Draft Stock

Breiden Fehoko believes Arch Manning being selected anywhere in the first five rounds of the NFL Draft would be evidence of a "nepo baby system."

"I say this with seriousness. If Arch Manning gets drafted anywhere in the first 5 rounds the NFL is a nepo baby system. Arch Manning is a bad football player can we start being real?" Fehoko wrote.

Fehoko's post came after Texas' 27-24 loss to Florida on Oct. 17, when Manning completed 14 of 20 passes for 173 yards and a touchdown.

Through six games this season, Manning has completed 106 of 166 passes (63.9%) for 1,295 yards, throwing 11 touchdowns and five interceptions.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Manning entered the season as one of the leading candidates to be the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, his performances so far have done little to strengthen his case, with some analysts even suggesting that another year in college could benefit him.

Manning struggled a lot in Texas' 27-24 loss to unranked Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two late interceptions proved costly. One was returned for a pick-six, while the other put the Sooners in position to kick the game-winning field goal.

His performance drew some harsh criticism from Jason Kirk of The Athletic as well, who went as far as calling Manning "college football's most average QB" in his 'Until Saturday' newsletter.

At the time, Kirk backed up his take with the numbers, citing Manning's passer rating as 143.31 compared with his calculated FBS average of 142.25 across 138 teams.

"'Joe Smith' fits Manning because, despite how frequently it has felt like he is the most promising or overrated or over-hated QB ever, he really just plays like a 'Joe Smith,'" Kirk wrote.

He was referring to Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian, who came to Manning's defense by suggesting that people might view the quarterback's performances differently if he were an ordinary player named "Joe Smith" playing for Texas.

Meanwhile, quarterbacks like Darian Mensah, Trinidad Chambliss, and Drew Mestemaker have been putting together strong performances. That makes it increasingly difficult for Manning to separate himself from the competition for the top spot.

Both organizations had backed Kelce's charitable efforts, and he wanted to help them reach more people.“[Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough] were the first two that really got on board to what my mission was and what I wanted to be a part of,” Kelce said in the same April 8 interview.He added that both organizations had helped him connect with the Kansas City community. articles.body:
We are still many months away from the 2027 NFL draft, but there has been some early buzz in the scouting community.

ESPN's Rich Cimini revealed that the New York Jets have been linked to Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr.

"CJ Carr is the name when you put your ear to the ground in the scouting circle; that's the name that has rumblings with the Jets," Cimini said on the "Jets Collective" podcast. "For what it's worth, there's rumblings."

Carr, 21, is in his third season with the Irish and second as a full-time starter. Before the 2026 college football season, Carr was included on every prominent QB award watch list.

The Jets have a clear and obvious need at the quarterback position. They're also armed with three first-round draft choices in the 2027 NFL draft.

ESPN New York's Jake Asman said general manager Darren Mougey has seen Carr in person twice during this college football season to date. The Jets also met with Carr when they visited the Irish Pro Day ahead of the 2026 NFL draft. He wasn't eligible for that class, but any extra touchpoints you can have with a player, the better.

ESPN senior NFL draft insider Mel Kiper Jr , released his top-25 big board this week. He included five quarterbacks inside his top-10.

Carr was ranked No. 8 overall on the big board and the fourth-ranked quarterback in this class:

"There's a lot to like in Carr's game. He's smart and processes quickly before and after the snap, which is part of the reason he has taken just two sacks all season. He's accurate to all levels and throws with anticipation. And while his arm strength is good but not great, he can cause conflict for defenses with his mobility. Carr can throw on the move or pick up a first down on the ground. Nothing phases him, and he's always in control. In short, Carr is pretty advanced in the key areas of NFL-level quarterback play," Kiper wrote.

Heading into the meat of Week 6 in the NFL, the Jets would have three picks inside the top-12 ( per Tankathon ):

11th overall (via the Indianapolis Colts )

The Jets will end up with whatever proves to be the better first-round choice between the Cowboys and the Green Bay Packers in 2027.

The Jets have a path to drafting Carr organically or having the opportunity to trade up for him with their ample draft capital.

We're still incredibly early in this process, but to hear that the Jets might already have an affinity for a player is interesting. The Jets owe it to themselves to do as much homework as possible on every possible arm that could be involved in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Not to be too hyperbolic, but this may be one of the most important drafts in franchise history. If the Jets were ever going to turn this around, the 2027 NFL draft has a chance to be a foundational piece of that change.

articles.body:
Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning entered the season as the favorite to go No. 1 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. But after another costly turnover in Saturday's loss to the Florida Gators, his own head coach wouldn't commit to him as the starter.

After the game, Manning responded to Steve Sarkisian's comments as he embraced the criticism and acknowledged that he needs to perform better.

Texas jumped out to a 17-3 lead over Florida on Saturday, but the Gators scored the next 24 points behind backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr., who was making his first career start, to pull off a 27-24 upset in Austin.

Manning completed 14 of 20 passes for 173 yards and a touchdown, but his late fumble essentially ended the game. That came one week after his late interception helped Oklahoma beat Texas.

After the loss, Sarkisian didn't rule out benching Manning when asked if he would consider a change at quarterback.

"We're not playing good offensive football right now, so everything is going to be evaluated," Sarkisian said, via On3 .

If Texas does decide to make a switch, redshirt freshman K.J. Lacey, a former four-star recruit, would be next in line.

Manning was asked about Sarkisian's comments after the game, and he didn't seem bothered by the idea of being evaluated.

"Yeah, I mean everyone's evaluated every week. That's how it is when you go to a school like this with elite players. Everyone's gotta get better and that starts with me," Manning said, via CJ Vogel of On Texas Football.

Manning has thrown for more than 250 yards in just one of his last five games and has turned the ball over in crucial moments in back-to-back games. The road doesn't get much easier for Texas as the team still has to face Ole Miss, Mississippi State, Missouri, and LSU over the next four weeks.

Needless to say, Manning will need to back up his words quickly if he wants to hold on to the starting job, because Texas is getting desperate.

Whether you're keeping up with your favorite NHL team's prospects or just enjoy watching minor league hockey, there are tons of great players in the AHL honing their craft and preparing for the big leagues.

The AHL is a fantastic development league, and that's demonstrated this season more than ever. Because its level of competition is higher than major-junior, teams pushed for a new agreement between the NHL and the CHL.

Previously, no 19-year-olds drafted out of a CHL league were allowed to be assigned to an AHL team. Thanks to the new agreement—which was almost certainly spurred on by the widening development options afforded due to CHL players now being permitted to play NCAA hockey—one 19-year-old drafted specifically in the first round from each NHL team can play in the AHL this season.

A couple of the players on this list are in the AHL because of that agreement; several others would've greatly benefited from it existing last season. All of the players on this list are going to be consistently and thoroughly challenged as the level of talent in the league continues to rise ever higher. It's up to them whether they rise to that challenge, but for those of us who are prospect heads, it's definitely going to make things even more entertaining than they already were.

This list is by no means exhaustive, but it's a great place to start. We're looking at three players from the Eastern Conference and three players from the Western Conference.

Kashawn Aitcheson — D, Hamilton Hammers (NYI)

New York Islanders prospect and defenseman Kashawn Aitcheson is spending this season with the AHL's newest team, the Hamilton Hammers. Don't be surprised if you see him as an injury call-up at some point this season, though; in addition to perfectly suiting the Islanders' preferred identity, Aitcheson's playing style feels like the perfect complement to a player like Matthew Schaefer. While he brings a strong physical presence, he can also more than keep up offensively, and it's a lot of fun to watch.

Last season Aitcheson co-captained the OHL's Barrie Colts with the next player on our list (spoiler alert), and put up 70 points in 56 games with a further 27 points in 19 playoff games. His hard-hitting, battling dimension gets discussed a lot, but his offensive game is greatly enjoyable. He's constantly engaged, closing gaps and forcing opponents to the outside, and at the same time he's anticipating the location of teammates to send off a pass, or finding the back of the net. It wouldn't be surprising to see him on the second power-play unit for the Islanders in the future (with Schaefer obviously running the first).

There are elements of his game that require refining before he makes the NHL full-time; specifically his decision-making when it comes to being a little too physical at the wrong time, as well as his defensive and passing choices. But that's exactly what his time in the AHL is for, and his overall engagement in the game bodes well for his ability to identify those needed changes and make them. He's also just a heck of a lot of fun to watch; Hammers fans will find themselves rooting for him straight away, if they aren't already doing so.

Cole Beaudoin — C, Hartford Wolf Pack (NYR)

Center Cole Beaudoin, drafted 24th overall by the Utah Mammoth in 2024, was traded to the New York Rangers last season as part of the larger Vincent Trocheck deal. His addition was a really nice step forward for a Rangers prospect pool that was less-than-impressive, as Beaudoin brings significant skill, particularly when it comes to complementing other skilled players on his line.

Beaudoin, the other former Barrie Colts captain—I swear this article doesn't contain multiple Barrie Colts products on purpose—put up 88 points in 54 games last season, as well as a further 29 points in 15 playoff games. It was beyond time for him to jump to the next level and further challenge himself.

Though he's played four NHL games this season, having been called up to fill in for forward Joe Veleno, Beaudoin did not record any points. He spent those games on the fourth line, and averaged 10-11 minutes in all but the last where he played 3:30. In Hartford he'll be playing regular minutes every night, and that's what he needs to learn how to best transition his strengths to professional hockey.

We can already see that he can transition those strengths; he recorded five points in his first two AHL games. He's cooled off a bit since, obviously, and currently sits at six points in four games, which feels like a pretty decent snapshot of the kind of player we expect him to be. It's still a small sample size, though—we've got a whole season ahead of us.

Bill Zonnon — C, Wilkes-Barre Scranton Penguins (PIT)

When Bill Zonnon arrived to the Wilkes-Barre Scranton Penguins after his last QMJHL season ended, he immediately fit in like a puzzle piece. Turned out he'd been studying Penguins game tape so that he would know the system when it came time for him to join the team. The way that he was able to apply what he'd learned from that studying immediately made me wish we'd had a chance to see him play the entire season in the AHL.

Thankfully, we get that chance this season—he turned 20 at the beginning of October, so he didn't require the 19-year-old exception. At the time of writing he's sitting at 5 points in 6 games, and it won't be at all surprising if those totals continue to trend upward.

Drafted 22nd overall in the 2025 NHL Draft, Zonnon put up 46 points in 35 games with the Blaineville-Boisbriand Armada of the QMJHL last season. He impressed despite being hampered by injury at multiple points in the season, showcasing excellent pace and passing abilities. His skating could use some refinement, but his fluidity with the puck—particularly the precision in his passing—is no doubt a facet of his game that the big club will be keeping a close eye on.

Caleb Desnoyers — C, Tucson Roadrunners (UTA)

QMJHL product Caleb Desnoyers, drafted 4th overall by the Utah Mammoth in 2025, is another 19-year-old exception. He won't turn 20 until right around the end of the regular season in April, but thanks to the new agreement he'll be spending that season sanding off the rough edges of his game against bigger and tougher opponents instead of developing bad habits in the Q.

The former Moncton Wildcats captain had 78 points (22 goals, 56 assists) in 45 regular season games last season. He added a further 25 points in 21 playoff games. It's extremely easy to look at that scoring pace, already a jump to 1.73 points-per-game from 1.5 the prior season, and assume that if he returned to the Q this year he'd explode even further offensively thanks to his constant engagement in play and the precision with which he finds teammates.

In the AHL, he won't find that quite so easy. Opponents are larger, more experienced, requiring more force and energy to beat. Desnoyers isn't the type of player to cheat for offense, which will serve him well, but to utilize his vision and tactical approach at the professional level, he needs to add more power and urgency to his game. The AHL requires that. It's going to be a lot of fun watching it develop.

Brady Martin — C, Milwaukee Admirals (NSH)

Last season, 2025 5th overall pick Brady Martin started out the year with the Nashville Predators, playing three NHL games. As he was 18, he couldn't be assigned to the AHL and wasn't ready for the NHL, so he was returned to major-junior hockey. This year, however, he's suiting up for the Milwaukee Admirals of the AHL as one of the players taking advantage of the new 19-year-old exception.

His season was undoubtedly a frustrating one; a shoulder injury limited him to only 24 games with the Soo Greyhounds (which he captained), and only a point-per-game pace after posting a 1.26 point-per-game pace during his draft season.

This wasn't entirely surprising; shoulder injuries take so long to return to form, particularly in hockey when they drive the foundation of so many skills. Can you imagine trying to shoot or pass a puck with an injured or less-than-recovered shoulder? Much less doing it as a physical, heavy-hitting player like Martin is. It also wasn't surprising, then, that he had a less-than-impressive preseason.

But that's what makes this season so exciting. Not only does he have a full, hopefully injury-free season ahead of him, he's going to continue his return to form and continue to look more like himself as time goes on, and he's going to do it against bigger, tougher opponents. It's such a great opportunity, particularly as his playing style of high pace and destructive yet productive hitting is perfectly suited for the AHL.

Dallas Stars prospect Emil Hemming is off to a slow start for the season, with no points in five games at time of writing. That said, it doesn't feel like much to worry about yet. Hemming also got off to a slow start last season, with no points through five AHL games before he was loaned to the Barrie Colts of the OHL (where he played with the aforementioned Kashawn Aitcheson). He would go on to put up 63 points in 46 games with the Colts, as well as a further 28 points in 21 playoff games. It was a significant jump from his 48 points in 60 games with the Colts the previous season, his first in North America.

Unlike every other player on this list, Hemming wasn't drafted out of the CHL. He was playing in the Finnish Liiga when the Stars selected him 29th overall in 2024 and then loaned to the OHL to further his development on North American ice. He did have the option to play in the AHL last season, but in opposition to the other players we've discussed, the OHL was a better place for him.

That's the main reason we're so excited to watch him this season. By all accounts, his time in the OHL last year saw his skating improve, and saw him showcase flashes of playmaking and dynamism. The big question is whether he can carry those forward. He's skilled in just about every area of the game; he just needs to learn to apply them at the pro level.
